_quantizer.method: weight-only, symmetric, per-output-channel round-to-nearest (RTN). For each nn.Linear weight W: s = max|W| per output row / (2^(b-1) - 1), then W := round(W/s).clamp * s. Applied in place to a freshly loaded float32 model.
_quantizer.what_is_NOT_quantized: nn.Embedding, LayerNorm, biases, and any module that is not nn.Linear. The per-model count of quantized Linear layers is recorded in the results file, because 'we quantized the model' is not a measurement and the module list is.
_quantizer.WHY_RTN_AND_THE_ASYMMETRY_THIS_CREATES: RTN is the weakest standard quantizer -- GPTQ and AWQ use calibration data and preserve behaviour better. So RTN is a WORST CASE. Surviving RTN implies surviving a real calibrated quantizer; FAILING RTN does NOT imply failing GPTQ or AWQ. Every negative result from this arm is scoped by that asymmetry, and it is registered now so the scope cannot be forgotten if the result is bad.
_quantizer.what_this_is_still_not: a real deployed quantized checkpoint, activation quantization, or a mixed-precision serving stack. It is weight rounding at two bit widths.
